title: Kolkata-Style Kathi Rolls at Home: A Five-Step Street-Food Classic
excerpt: Paratha, egg, spiced chicken and a crisp salad wrapped in wax paper — IndulgExpress's five-step method for the Kolkata street-food classic.
body:
• The Kolkata kathi roll — born on the city's streets, where cooks rolled dough onto a griddle, cracked an egg over it and wrapped spicy fillings in paper — takes five steps and about 35 minutes of active cooking at home.
  • The signature moves: an egg-lined paratha, chicken marinated in tandoori masala, cumin, coriander, lemon juice and mustard oil, and a crisp cucumber-onion-carrot salad with chaat masala.
  • The payoff: this recipe makes five rolls — perfect for a family dinner, and the chicken filling works for meal prep all week. Every spice listed is stocked at any Indian grocery in the US; make the parathas ahead and freeze them for fast assembly.

The kathi roll is Kolkata's answer to the question of how to eat dinner with one hand. Named for the kati — the bamboo skewers on which the meat was originally roasted — it became a street-food institution when Kolkata's vendors started rolling dough onto flat griddles in front of customers, cracking an egg onto it, piling on spicy fillings, and wrapping the whole thing in paper, served piping hot in minutes. It has since travelled to menus of Indian restaurants around the world. Here is how to make it at home, following IndulgExpress's five-step method.

The paratha

Combine all-purpose flour and salt in a sieve, then add oil and water to form a smooth dough. Let it rest for 15 minutes, then divide it into five portions and flatten each into a disk ready for frying. The rest matters — it relaxes the gluten so the parathas cook up tender rather than tough.

The filling

Blend chopped chicken with turmeric, chilli powder, tandoori masala, ground cumin, ground coriander, lemon juice, mustard oil and salt, then cook in canola oil for 15 minutes, adding tomato paste halfway through. The mustard oil is the Kolkata signature — don't skip it.

The egg lining

Oil your griddle and set a paratha on it. Break an egg onto the paratha and spread it around, then flip so the egg cooks all the way through. This is what separates a kathi roll from a plain chicken wrap: the thin, savory egg layer fused to the inside of the flatbread.

The salad

Chop cucumber and onion into thin slices, grate some carrots, and finely chop green chilli and fresh coriander. Mix everything in a bowl — this fresh, crisp layer is what cuts through the richness of the filling.

Assemble and wrap

Spread tomato and chilli sauce on the egg-lined flatbread, layer on the salad and the sautéed chicken, shower with chaat masala, and wrap firmly in wax paper. Serve hot.

Diaspora kitchen notes

Everything here is available at any Indian grocery: mustard oil, chaat masala, tandoori masala, wax paper. For weeknight speed, make a batch of the parathas on the weekend and freeze them between sheets of parchment; the chicken filling also reheats well, so one cook session covers lunch rolls for days. Want a vegetarian version? Marinate paneer or mushrooms with the same spice blend — the technique doesn't change.
